title: security(rbac): enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging hardening
author: Ava Chen
ci_summary: CI: lint ✓, unit tests ✓, integration tests ✓, e2e tests ✓ (one flaky auth-test rerun passed), infra checks ✓, security-scan ✓. Rerun recorded for integration/auth-suite due to timeout on first attempt.
description:
Motivation: Customers in regulated environments require stronger guarantees that KMS keys and encrypted artifacts do not leave configured regions and that RBAC v2 policies produce reliable audit events for key access. This PR enforces KMS region pinning at the RBAC policy evaluation layer and hardens audit logging to include key residency assertions and request trace ids. Changes include a policy-level validation step (opt-out gated by feature flag for older deployments), additional audit fields emitted for KMS operations, tests and migration guidance, and a rollout plan with canary rate limits.

What I changed: 1) Added policy enforcement: RBAC v2 now verifies that any KMS key referenced by a request matches the resource residency constraints declared on the project/route. Requests that violate residency are rejected with 403 and a structured error indicating the mismatch. 2) Audit logging: KMS access events now include kms_key_id, kms_key_region, effective_policy_id, evaluated_constraints, and request_trace_id. Logs are emitted to audit-log topic and local structured JSON logger for on-prem. 3) Feature flag: security.kms_region_enforcement (default: on for new installs, off for upgrades) and an admin migration job that can be used to audit current resources prior to enabling. 4) Tests: unit, integration, and a simulated Dedicated/Private scenario with mocked KMS endpoints. 5) Docs and release notes: added rollout/rollback steps and a Linear ticket reference.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for policy evaluation and edge cases - [x] Integration tests for KMS call paths and audit emission - [x] Migration script + dry-run mode - [x] Docs update in redwood-docs - [x] Security review and threat modeling completed - [x] Ops runbook for enabling the feature in Dedicated/Private environments

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag (already gated). 2) Canary enable for 5% of tenant traffic with real KMS verification for 48h. 3) Monitor audit logs and errors; if error rate > 0.5% for canary, rollback. 4) If stable, escalate to 100% over 24h with staged tenant cohorts.

Backout: Disable security.kms_region_enforcement or flip to dry-run; run migration job with report mode to identify offending resources.

Related: ENG-4932, SEC-210.
